_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written from scratch.
name: Audiobookshelf
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Audiobookshelf is an audiobook and podcast server with a web player, progress sync and apps for phones. The egg builds it from its source and creates the root account with a password made at install.
startup: cd audiobookshelf && m=index.js; [ ! -f dist-server/index.js ] || m=dist-server/index.js; NODE_ENV=production PORT={{SERVER_PORT}} HOST=0.0.0.0 CONFIG_PATH=/home/container/config METADATA_PATH=/home/container/metadata exec node $m

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Audiobookshelf: builds the chosen release from its GitHub source (it
# publishes no Linux build) with Node.js 24 from nodejs.org, checked against
# Node's published checksums, into audiobookshelf/. The database and
# settings (config/), metadata and the books and podcasts are never touched;
# the app is only replaced once the new build is complete.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=advplyr/audiobookshelf
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
# gh_tag <latest|tag> prints the release's tag; returns 1 when there's no
# such release, 2 when GitHub can't be reached.
gh_tag() {
    local out
    out=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$1" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; return 0; }
    case "$out" in *"has no release"* | *"no releases"*) return 1 ;; *) return 2 ;; esac
}
offline="GitHub can't be reached right now, or is limiting downloads. Reinstall to try again in a few minutes."
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=x64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Audiobookshelf can't be built for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
case "$version" in latest|v*) ;; *) version="v$version" ;; esac
rc=0; tag=$(gh_tag "$version") || rc=$?
if [ "$rc" = 1 ]; then
    latest=$(gh_tag latest) || fail "$offline"
    fail "Audiobookshelf has no version ${VERSION}. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as ${latest#v}."
fi
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || fail "$offline"
version=$tag

tmp=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$tmp" .raptor-old && mkdir -p "$tmp"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp" .raptor-old' EXIT
mkdir -p config metadata audiobooks podcasts
# The build writes caches to the temp folder, and the install container's
# /tmp is a small in-memory one: use a folder in the server's instead.
mkdir -p "$tmp/tmp"
export TMPDIR="$tmp/tmp" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$tmp/cache"
export npm_config_cache="$tmp/npm" npm_config_update_notifier=false npm_config_fund=false npm_config_audit=false

# Node.js to build with (and to create the admin account below).
node_dist=https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v24.x
node_sums=$(curl -fsSL --retry 3 "$node_dist/SHASUMS256.txt") || fail "nodejs.org can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
read -r node_sum node_file < <(grep -E "  node-v[0-9.]+-linux-$arch\.tar\.xz$" <<<"$node_sums") || fail "nodejs.org has no Node.js 24 for this CPU."
use_node() {
    [ -x "$tmp/node/bin/node" ] && return
    echo "Downloading ${node_file%.tar.xz} to build with"
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$tmp/node.tar.xz" "$node_dist/$node_file" || fail "The Node.js download failed. Reinstall to try again."
    [ "$(sha256sum "$tmp/node.tar.xz" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$node_sum" ] || fail "The Node.js download didn't match its checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir -p "$tmp/node"
    tar -xJf "$tmp/node.tar.xz" -C "$tmp/node" --strip-components=1
    rm -f "$tmp/node.tar.xz"
    export PATH="$tmp/node/bin:$PATH"
}

if [ -f audiobookshelf/.raptor-version ] && [ "$(cat audiobookshelf/.raptor-version)" = "$version" ]; then
    echo "Audiobookshelf $version is already installed."
else
    use_node
    echo "Downloading Audiobookshelf $version"
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$tmp/src.tar.gz" "https://github.com/$repo/archive/refs/tags/$version.tar.gz" || fail "The download failed. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir -p "$tmp/src"
    tar -xzf "$tmp/src.tar.gz" -C "$tmp/src" --strip-components=1
    rm -f "$tmp/src.tar.gz"
    cd "$tmp/src"
    echo "Building the web app (this takes a few minutes)"
    # Its minifier starts a worker for every CPU, each with its own memory,
    # which overflows the install's limit (the server's memory, at least
    # 1 GB, with no swap). Minifying in the build itself, with a capped
    # heap, fits in 1 GB.
    sed -i 's/^  build: {},$/  build: { terser: { parallel: false } },/' client/nuxt.config.js
    export NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=768
    (cd client && npm ci --loglevel=error > "$tmp/build.log" 2>&1 && npm run generate >> "$tmp/build.log" 2>&1) || { tail -n 30 "$tmp/build.log"; fail "Audiobookshelf's web app didn't build. Reinstall to try again."; }
    echo "Building the server"
    if grep -q '"build:server"' package.json; then
        { npm ci --include=dev --ignore-scripts --loglevel=error && npm run build:server && rm -rf node_modules; } > "$tmp/build.log" 2>&1 || { tail -n 30 "$tmp/build.log"; fail "Audiobookshelf's server didn't build. Reinstall to try again."; }
    fi
    unset NODE_OPTIONS
    npm ci --omit=dev --loglevel=error > "$tmp/build.log" 2>&1 || { tail -n 30 "$tmp/build.log"; fail "Audiobookshelf's dependencies didn't install. Reinstall to try again."; }
    mkdir -p "$tmp/app/client"
    mv client/dist "$tmp/app/client/dist"
    for e in index.js package.json package-lock.json server dist-server node_modules; do [ ! -e "$e" ] || mv "$e" "$tmp/app/"; done
    echo "$version" > "$tmp/app/.raptor-version"
    cd /mnt/server
    # ffmpeg and ffprobe, which Audiobookshelf downloads itself next to the
    # app, move to config/ (where it also looks) so an update keeps them.
    for b in ffmpeg ffprobe libnusqlite3.so libnusqlite3.so.ver; do [ ! -f "audiobookshelf/$b" ] || mv -f "audiobookshelf/$b" config/; done
    [ ! -e audiobookshelf ] || mv audiobookshelf .raptor-old
    mv "$tmp/app" audiobookshelf
fi

# A new Audiobookshelf lets whoever opens it first create the root account.
# On the first install, start it once here to create root with a random
# password. That first start also downloads the ffmpeg Audiobookshelf uses.
if [ ! -f config/absdatabase.sqlite ]; then
    use_node
    password=$(head -c 18 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=')
    port=13378
    # Audiobookshelf saves full paths in its database, so it runs from
    # /home/container here too, the server's folder when it runs.
    if [ ! -e /home/container ]; then mkdir -p /home && ln -s /mnt/server /home/container; fi
    [ /home/container -ef /mnt/server ] || fail "The install can't reach the server's folder as /home/container."
    (cd /home/container/audiobookshelf && NODE_ENV=production PORT=$port HOST=127.0.0.1 CONFIG_PATH=/home/container/config METADATA_PATH=/home/container/metadata \
        exec node "$( [ -f dist-server/index.js ] && echo dist-server/index.js || echo index.js )") > "$tmp/first.log" 2>&1 &
    pid=$!
    base="http://127.0.0.1:$port/audiobookshelf"
    # Requests to it go through /usr/bin/curl: the install's curl counts
    # every refused connection while it starts as a failed download.
    lcurl=/usr/bin/curl
    for _ in $(seq 300); do
        $lcurl -fs -o /dev/null "$base/status" && break
        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
        sleep 1
    done
    ok=0
    $lcurl -fsS -o /dev/null -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$(jq -n --arg p "$password" '{newRoot: {username: "root", password: $p}}')" "$base/init" &&
        [ "$($lcurl -fsS "$base/status" | jq -r .isInit)" = true ] && ok=1
    kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$pid" || true
    for b in ffmpeg ffprobe libnusqlite3.so libnusqlite3.so.ver; do [ ! -f "audiobookshelf/$b" ] || mv -f "audiobookshelf/$b" config/; done
    if [ "$ok" != 1 ]; then
        tail -n 30 "$tmp/first.log"
        rm -f config/absdatabase.sqlite*
        fail "Audiobookshelf didn't start to create its root account. Reinstall to try again."
    fi
    echo "The admin account is root, with the password $password. Change it in Audiobookshelf's settings."
fi
echo "Installed Audiobookshelf $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Audiobookshelf version to install, such as 2.37.2, or latest.
